title: SummitCore activation playbook and evaluation checklist
body:
Executive summary:

This playbook documents the 4-week SummitCore pilot activation window for the Retail Conversational Assistant. Purpose is to validate integration, operational characteristics (latency, throughput, cost), and quality signals against business KPIs so SummitCore can make a go/no-go decision on Dedicated capacity. The document is intended for internal SEs, SummitCore technical leads, and customer success.

Pilot objectives (primary):
- Demonstrate end-to-end integration between SummitCore backend and Redwood hosted API with schema-enforced tool-calls.
- Achieve 95th-percentile generation latency <= 450ms for 256-token requests under baseline load (50 RPS burstable).
- Maintain average cost-per-1000-tokens within 20% of Redwood suggested config for the chosen model variant.
- Pass quality baseline: user-facing answer correctness >= 88% (measured on the provided 250-query eval set) and hallucination rate < 6% on illusions benchmark.

Success criteria (measurable acceptance):
1) Integration readiness
- API handshake: successful token-based authentication and example query/response validated by SummitCore engineering (confluence page linked).
- Schema validation: tool-calling and structured JSON outputs parsed by SummitCore staging pipeline without schema errors for 98% of test requests.

2) Performance & reliability
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms for 256-token profile, p99 <= 900ms during steady-state 30 RPS traffic
- Throughput: sustained 50 RPS for 30 minutes with no 5xx errors
- Error budget: <= 0.5% 5xx across pilot window
- Failover exercise: automatic fallback to smaller model variant completes within target SLO (fallback time <= 60s) when simulated capacity constraints are injected.

3) Quality & safety
- Eval set: 250 user queries provided by SummitCore; automated scoring shows >= 88% correctness (semantic match + fuzzy scoring)
- Hallucination/Policy: hallucination rate < 6% and zero policy-triggered abusive responses in sampled 1k logs
- Safety filters: content moderation rules enforced at request ingress; false-positive rate < 2% on curated good-queries set.

4) Operational handover
- Monitoring configured: per-route dashboards created in Redwood Console, with token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency charts and alerting thresholds.
- Runbook & playbooks: incident runbook validated by SRE and SummitCore on-call for at least one simulated outage scenario.
- Signoff: SummitCore technical and product leads confirm acceptance via signoff checklist.

Pilot scope (what we will / won't do):
- In scope: hosted API integration, model variant testing (standard/quantized), Console dashboards, basic KV-prefix caching evaluation, canary rollout to 10% of summit staging traffic, UAT evaluation using SummitCore-supplied prompts.
- Out of scope: private VPC deployment, custom kernel engineering, long-term cost optimization (that will be part of post-pilot recommendations).

Data & access checklist (customer action items):
- API keys: SummitCore to provide a deploy key and a separate telemetry key for metrics ingestion (scoped).
- Example dataset: canonical 250-query eval set (CSV) and 1k production-sampled anonymized conversations for quality sampling.
- Endpoint allowlist: SummitCore network team to provide CIDR ranges if IP allowlisting required.
- PII handling: confirm whether training/eval data contains PII; if so, provide data classification and redaction requirements.

Technical validation plan (week-by-week):
Week 0 (pre-kickoff prep, 3 days):
- Accounts & keys exchanged, staging environment prepared, schema contract agreed. Owner: SummitCore infra + Maya.
Week 1 (integration + smoke tests):
- REST integration, tool-calls, sample prompts, initial latency numbers at low load. Provide integration checklist to SummitCore. Owner: Liam.
Week 2 (load & quality):
- Load tests to 50 RPS, KV caching toggles, collect token-cost estimates. Run eval set and surface detailed quality report. Owner: Priya.
Week 3 (rollout & resiliency):
- Canary 10-30%, failover injection, alerting configured. Finalize runbooks and training. Owner: Diego.
Week 4 (handover & signoff):
- Consolidate metrics, present to SummitCore leadership, complete signoff checklist. Owner: Hannah.

Workshop agenda (first workshop / 90 minutes):
- 00:00–00:10: Introductions & objectives (Maya)
- 00:10–00:25: Integration contract review (REST endpoints, auth, schema) (Liam)
- 00:25–00:45: Eval set & quality rubric walkthrough (Priya)
- 00:45–01:00: Performance targets & test harness (load profile, tooling) (Diego)
- 01:00–01:20: Operational dashboards & runbook preview (Hannah)
- 01:20–01:30: Open Q&A and action items recap

Acceptance tests (automated and manual):
- Auth smoke: curl sample request with deploy key, expect 200 and valid JSON schema (automated).
- Tool-call contract: sample 50 requests containing tool invocation; 98% must parse into external catalog (automated).
- Load test: k6 script to ramp to 50 RPS over 5 minutes and hold for 30 minutes; assert p95 < 450ms and error rate < 0.5% (automated).
- Eval run: automated scoring pipeline to run 250-case eval and produce pass/fail (automated).
- UX review: SummitCore product reviews 30 sampled responses for subjective quality (manual).

Risk register (top 5 risks + mitigations):
1) Unexpected latency spike under caching-disabled scenarios. Mitigation: enable prefix caching and rerun targeted tests; schedule kernel-config consult with runtime team.
2) Data access delays from SummitCore (missing eval set). Mitigation: run fallback synthetic eval and mark quality metrics as provisional.
3) Schema mismatch on tool-calls. Mitigation: immediate contract stub and shared JSON schema; hold rapid pairing session.
4) Cost > target due to verbose generation. Mitigation: tune decoding settings (top-p/top-k), token limit guardrails, and try quantized model variant.
5) Security policy flags causing blocked queries. Mitigation: review policy rules with SummitCore security and create allowlist exceptions for staging.

Deliverables (SE team):
- Integration checklist (completed)
- Performance & cost report (PDF)
- Quality evaluation report with example failure cases (CSV + notes)
- Final handoff slide deck and signoff checklist

Signoff template (for SummitCore leads):
- Technical integration: Accept / Accept with notes / Reject
- Performance SLOs met: Yes / No (attach metrics)
- Quality threshold met: Yes / No (attach eval report)
- Operational readiness & runbooks: Yes / No
- Final go recommendation: Proceed to Dedicated / Extend Pilot / Stop

Operational notes and quick tips:
- If p95 spikes > 700ms during testing, reduce batch window and re-run; look for long-tail KV cache misses.
- Use the Console tracing hook for request-level debugging; enable sample-level logging during Week 2 only to minimize cost.

Open questions for SummitCore (to be resolved during week 0):
- Are there regulatory constraints requiring logging retention limits or on-prem telemetry?
- Which internal team owns the UAT signoff? Product or Data Science?
- Will SummitCore provide a sanitized 1k conversation sample or do we need to synthesize?

Contacts:
- SE lead (owner): Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)
- Performance lead: Liam O'Rourke (liam@redwood.ai)
- Quality lead: Priya Nambiar (priya@redwood.ai)
- Runtime/resiliency: Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.ai)
- Customer Success: Hannah Park (hannah@redwood.ai)

Notes / version history:
- 2025-01-10: initial draft created by Maya
- 2025-01-12: added load-test scripts and failover plan (Liam)
- 2025-01-15: updated acceptance thresholds after alignment call with SummitCore (Priya)

Appendix: quick checklist (one-liner items)
- [ ] keys exchanged
- [ ] eval set uploaded
- [ ] schema validated
- [ ] k6 load script run
- [ ] console dashboards created
- [ ] runbooks reviewed

End of document
